title: Microsoft Attracts $115B in Orders for First High-Grade Bond Sale Since 2017
summary:
Investor demand for Microsoft's current fundraising effort reached $115B, making it the sixth largest orderbook for an investment-grade bond sale in history. The company is seeking to raise at least $25B through a 10-part U.S. dollar offering, the first time the software giant has issued domestic high-grade debt since January 2017.

The notes include maturities ranging from 2 to 40 years, with proceeds slated for general corporate purposes and capital expenditures. The move reflects a surge in AI infrastructure costs; Microsoft recently reported $45.2B in quarterly AI spending and projects that AI-related capex and leases could reach roughly $170B by 2027. Other tech rivals including Alphabet, Amazon and Meta have similarly turned to debt and equity markets to fund their data center expansions this year.

MICROSOFT PREPARES AT LEAST $25 BILLION BOND SALE, ITS FIRST SINCE 2017

$MSFT is looking to raise at least $25B through a 10-part U.S. bond offering, as it joins other major tech companies tapping debt markets to finance the AI infrastructure buildout.

The offering would mark Microsoft's first major bond sale in nine years, when it raised $17B in 2017.

Despite holding a rare AAA credit rating and generating substantial cash flow, Microsoft had remained on the sidelines while Alphabet, Amazon and Meta turned to large bond offerings over the past year.

The bonds are expected to have maturities ranging from 2 to 40 years, with proceeds available for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures.

The move follows Microsoft's fiscal Q1 earnings yesterday and comes just months after Alphabet raised $25B in its August bond sale.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Hyperscalers and data center developers have sold more than $313B of investment-grade bonds this year
selectedTweets.text:
Bloomberg: Microsoft is returning to the US bond market for the first time since its $17B sale in 2017, seeking at least $25B across up to 10 tranches.

Its 40-year note is priced near Alphabet’s and Amazon’s long bonds despite Microsoft’s stronger AAA rating, which suggests the flood of AI debt is lifting borrowing costs for everyone.

Hyperscalers and data center developers have sold more than $313B of investment-grade bonds this year, almost 3 times 2025’s total, pushing global bond sales to a record $6.61T.
